reviews.notes: Primary-source check supports the Q2 software figures, BTC holdings, debt, preferred liquidation preference and separate common/preferred ATM programs. Capital analysis correctly distinguishes common dilution from senior preferred claims, but it never reconciles a fully diluted common denominator across convertibles, preferred conversion features and issued common stock. Add a retail war-room covering BTC gap risk, mNAV slippage, position sizing, overnight financing announcements and an explicit no-chase rule.

The official Q2 deck supports $1.22B revenue, $207.8M adjusted EBITDA, $238.3M SBC and Q3 subscription guidance; customer assets are correctly excluded from corporate NAV. The 65.5x EV/EBITDA claim lacks a numeric peer or historical comparison, and fully diluted exposure after SBC is not reconciled. TP1 at $199.18 is neither a displayed resistance nor independently justified and reproduces a 1.60R batch target. Add a gap/liquidity/slippage/sizing/no-chase war-room.

The Q2 shareholder letter and 10-Q support revenue, production, energy cost, pledged BTC and debt. The NAV row lists assets and debt without a dated BTC price, computed residual NAV, per-share value or current-equity comparison. The later $600M BTC-backed financing is discussed without its own accession-specific financing finding, and diluted exposure is unreconciled. Both targets are formulaic 1.60R/2.30R rather than displayed resistance. Add retail gap and collateral-liquidation controls.

Primary filings support the revenue decline, negative adjusted EBITDA, debt load and affirmative material-weakness risk. The crypto-NAV framework is not calculated per diluted share and supplies no dated BTC assumption. The $12.0782 stop is a mechanical 0.60 ATR level rather than a displayed support, while both targets sit beyond listed resistance and reproduce batch R multiples. Reconcile dilution and add a retail plan for BTC gaps, thin overnight books, slippage and no-chase behavior.

Official Q1 and July operating sources support product/mining revenue, losses, hashrate, treasury and the September 3 veto. The proposed NAV omits dated BTC/ETH prices, unrestricted cash, ADS ratio reconciliation and a computed per-ADS value. The older October 424B5 finding does not state exact security, amount and completed status; fully diluted ADS exposure is absent. Geometry is correctly dormant around earnings, but the dossier still needs an ADR-specific liquidity, gap, slippage, sizing and no-chase war-room.

The Q2 release and 10-Q support ETH holdings, staking revenue, token losses and the June common-plus-warrant financing. The $1.42B/217.0M NAV row does not subtract liabilities, compute diluted NAV or reprice the warrants; the older 424B5 is described generically. The $8.4142 stop and $9.3133/$9.5554 targets are not tied to displayed structures and reproduce 0.75 ATR plus 1.60R/2.30R geometry. Add ETH overnight-gap, wrapper-liquidity, slippage, sizing and no-chase rules.

The May 10-Q and August treasury 8-K support the reporting-boundary warning, ETH holdings, staking percentage and non-GAAP run-rate nature of projected revenue. The NAV discussion never computes common NAV after the $350M preferred claim or supplies numeric ETH/staking downside cases. The September 2025 prospectus finding is not security- and amount-specific, and diluted common exposure is not reconciled. Add a war-room for ETH gaps, staking liquidity, preferred overhang, slippage and no-chase sizing.

The Q2 exhibit and 10-Q support revenue, EBITDA, FCF, mine guidance, net cash and the post-acquisition share count. The 13.8x EV/EBITDA denominator is not dated or explicitly trailing/forward, and the stated lower-metal-price scenario contains no metal-price, cost or FCF sensitivity. The 1.0285B issued-share count is not reconciled to fully diluted exposure. Trade levels map to observed support/resistance, but the retail section must address commodity gaps, miner liquidity, slippage, sizing and no chase after metal spikes.

The official exhibit supports Q2 revenue, production, FCF, inventory and rising AISC. An A- grade is not adequately reconciled with 10.8x EV/EBITDA measured during an exceptional $63.98 realized silver quarter and a 22% AISC increase. The normalized-silver scenario has no numeric price or FCF output. Targets $25.23/$26.56 are not displayed resistance and exactly reproduce 1.60R/2.30R. Add a silver-gap, Mexico-event, slippage, sizing and no-chase war-room.

Primary sources support pre-merger Q2 results, post-merger production/AISC guidance and South Railroad capital. The A- grade mixes a pre-merger quarter with a much larger post-merger company without a reconstructed pro-forma quality score. Project budgets are not a mine NAV scenario, and the 9.5x denominator is not dated. The 378.1M-share merger issuance lacks its own transaction filing row and convertibles are not reconciled. The 0.60 ATR stop and 2.30R second target are partly synthetic. Add a retail merger/metal-gap war-room.

The Q2 exhibit and 10-Q verify revenue, EBITDA, capex, interest expense, guidance and continuing material weakness; shelf and terminated-merger documents are classified correctly. Valuation labels the stock premium without giving numeric neocloud or infrastructure peers, and the dossier does not reconcile fully diluted equity exposure alongside the liability stack. Technical levels align with displayed structure. Add a retail war-room for financing gaps, concentrated-customer headlines, thin after-hours execution, slippage, sizing and no chase.

Official fiscal Q4 sources support revenue, fit-out mix, adjusted EBITDA, SBC, contracted capacity and balance-sheet amounts. Peer valuation comparisons are qualitative only. The resale S-3 finding omits exact registered amount and holder status, while warrants and preferred conversion are not rolled into a fully diluted denominator. The $25.7775 stop is a 0.60 ATR construct rather than a cited support. Add a construction-financing gap, liquidity, slippage, sizing and no-chase war-room.

The direct Q2 release supports revenue, AI-cloud mix, ARR, margin and prepayments; filings distinguish completed common issuance, converts, ATM capacity and the proposed $4.5B notes. Valuation denominators and comparison dates are not explicit and no numeric neocloud peer set is shown. The preliminary 424B5 finding omits exact terms, diluted exposure is unreconciled, and targets beyond the sole $229.47 resistance reproduce 1.60R/2.30R. Add a prepayment/financing gap and no-chase retail plan.

The official release and filings support current HPC revenue, construction timing, the completed 47.4M-share offering and correct non-duplication of preliminary prospectuses. Trailing sales multiples are not enough for a 2027-2028 lease story; no discounted contract/capex scenario or numeric peer comparison is supplied. Roughly 80.9M warrant shares and converts are not reconciled into diluted shares. The $15.5325 stop is a mechanical 0.60 ATR level below displayed supports. Add construction-gap, slippage, sizing and no-chase controls.

The Q2 filing verifies revenue, negative adjusted EBITDA, restricted cash, borrowings and warrant liability; the dossier correctly refuses to net project cash as free liquidity. Trailing multiples provide no numeric scenario for converting optional or under-construction megawatts into equity value. Warrant liability is disclosed without fully diluted share exposure. The $15.5098 stop is exactly 0.60 ATR and not tied to displayed support. Add a project-financing gap, low-liquidity slippage, small-size and no-chase war-room.

The earnings exhibit and filings support Q2 results, project delivery timing, nonrecourse debt and the $1B ATM split between sold and remaining capacity. The valuation lacks a discounted project-NOI scenario or numeric power/hosting peer comparison. ATM issuance is not reconciled into a fully diluted denominator. The $81.5616 stop is a 0.60 ATR construct rather than displayed support. Add parent-versus-project liquidity, BTC gap, slippage, sizing and no-chase instructions.

Primary sources support colocation revenue, billing capacity, capex and the August debt facilities. The valuation has no numeric hosting peer or discounted leased-versus-billing-capacity comparison. Financing-linked warrant classes are disclosed without security quantities or fully diluted exposure. The $16.7099 stop and $18.6342/$19.1523 targets are mechanical 0.60 ATR and 1.60R/2.30R levels, not displayed structures. Add a financing/headline-gap, liquidity, slippage, sizing and no-chase war-room.

The FY2026 10-K supports revenue, impairment, cash, restricted cash and debt, and the dossier correctly enforces a filing-data veto. Publication still contains aggregate fields explicitly described as superseded, so point-in-time data integrity is unresolved. Contracted ARR lacks a recognized-revenue/downside valuation scenario. Two older 424B5 findings do not identify exact securities and amounts, and ATM dilution is unreconciled. Keep all levels inactive and add a retail war-room only after the bundle is rebuilt.

The official Q2 exhibit verifies revenue, GAAP margins, cash flow and raised guidance; SEC treatment correctly avoids inventing an ATM. The operating thesis, grade separation and technical structure are coherent. The remaining valuation comparison is qualitative: add numeric industrial-power peers or Bloom history to explain 20.7x EV/revenue and 153.6x EV/EBITDA. A retail war-room must also cover post-earnings gaps, order-book liquidity, slippage, reduced sizing at premium multiples and a no-chase condition.

The direct earnings exhibit supports adjusted EPS, raised guidance and operating catalysts; filings correctly classify both S-3ASRs as capacity, not issuance. Valuation cites utility and merchant history without numeric comparables. The $279.2408 stop is a 0.60 ATR budget rather than a displayed support, and the second target is not tied to listed resistance. Add a war-room for outage/integration gaps, liquidity around power headlines, slippage, sizing and no chase.

The Q2 exhibit and 10-Q support adjusted EBITDA, FCF guidance, hedge coverage, debt and repurchases; valuation uses appropriate power-sector measures and the grade/trade distinction is defensible. The $146.204 TP1 is not a displayed resistance and reproduces a 1.60R template, although the stop and TP2 are structural. Replace TP1 with an observed level or explicit scenario rationale. Add a retail war-room for hedge/commodity gaps, slippage, position size and no chasing power headlines.

The official release and SEC filings verify orders, revenue, margins, backlog, cash flow and the $2.6B straight-debt issuance; valuation, grade integrity and technical levels are internally coherent, and debt is not mislabeled as dilution. The only blocker is mandatory retail execution coverage: spell out earnings/order gap risk, liquidity and slippage near a four-digit share price, reduced unit sizing, event timing and a no-chase rule after backlog headlines.
